title: Low-latency dequant elision and attention-hint routing for prefill/ decode
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Reduce per-request latency and CPU/GPU memory churn caused by eager dequant/copy operations in INT8/FP8 paths during prefill (KV warmup) and streaming decode.

Background: We currently dequantize early in several execution paths to simplify attention kernels and upstream ops. That produces unnecessary copies for many workloads where downstream kernels can operate on quantized buffers or where dequantization can be deferred until the last possible moment. During prefill (long-context KV population) and streaming decode (microbatches), these copies amplify latency spikes and increase token cost.

Proposal: Implement a light-weight "dequant elision" layer + attention-hint router that: (1) tracks compatibility signatures for kernels (which kernels accept quantized tensors and which require FP tensors), (2) forwards an "attention hint" based on token-length/head-usage/profile to select quantization-friendly attention kernels where possible, and (3) defers or avoids dequantization for tensors that can remain quantized through attention and matmul sequences.

Key components:
- Kernel capability registry: small table of kernel features (accepts_int8, accepts_fp8, requires_fp32_accumulation, supports_zero_copy_kv). Populated from kernel metadata at startup and during model onboarding.
- Attention-hint router: runtime heuristic that uses request metadata (sequence length, is_prefill, deterministic decode vs sample, head sparsity hint) to route work to the best kernel variant.
- Dequant elision policy engine: per-request policy that decides: keep-quantized, delayed-dequant, eager-dequant. Policies chosen based on latency SLO, memory pressure, and fallback compatibility.
- Zero-copy bridging for KV cache: when possible, store KV in quantized format and expose a quantized view to downstream kernels to avoid copies between prefill and decode phases.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Correctness: some kernels require FP accumulation to match numeric stability; the policy must fall back reliably.
- Complexity: introduces more kernel variants and routing logic; must be measured against added scheduling overhead.
- Observability: need telemetry for counts of elisions, fallback events, and latency impact.

Expected benefits:
- Latency reduction on mixed workloads (prefill heavy + streaming decode): 6–18% P99 improvement in microbench spike tests.
- Reduced GPU memory churn and fewer transient host<->device copies for large-context prefill.
- Lower token-cost for hosted customers via reduced CPU overhead and better batching.

Non-goals: Full automated rewriting of model graphs or replacing compiler-level quantization passes. This work is focused on runtime routing and copy elimination within the serving runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel capability registry implemented and surfaced to runtime planner
Attention-hint router routes >80% of compatible requests to quantized-friendly kernels in benchmarked scenarios
Dequant elision policy avoids at least one host<->device copy per prefill request on targeted workloads
Automated fallbacks occur with observed telemetry and no correctness regressions in unit and integration tests
End-to-end microbenchmark: P99 latency improvement >= 6% on prefill+decode mix (internal eval harness)
comments: 2026-02-22 - Spike: implemented minimal capability registry. Measured kernel metadata extraction cost ~0.4ms on bootstrap. - Asha

2026-02-27 - Microbench: naive elision (skip dequant for attention when kernel accepts int8) gave 9% median latency improvement but regressed a small subset of fp32-sensitive tests. Added numeric tolerance checks. - Miguel

2026-03-02 - Design review with ML infra: agreed on per-model opt-in flag during onboarding; default remains safe (no elision) until we have telemetry. Required audit log when elision enabled for private deployments. - Notes linked: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/RT-105431
2026-03-05 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9482. Implements capability registry + routing stub. Needs unit tests for fallback paths. - Miguel

2026-03-08 - Bench run (nvidia-a100, 8-token prefill + streaming decode): P99 improved 11% for bert-like attention shape; cost of routing ~0.2ms per request. Logging added to measure elision/fallback ratio. - Benchmark artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/rt/105431/2026-03-08
2026-03-10 - Security/Compliance note: For Private deployments, KMS-backed models may opt out of telemetry; ensure elision correctness does not rely on remote telemetry. - Security (L. Chen)

2026-03-11 - Blocker discovered: one fused attention kernel incorrectly reported accepts_int8=true while internally requiring fp32 accumulation for overflow cases. Disabled auto-elision for that kernel variant and scheduled kernel fix. - Miguel
